story.title: The first shirt sponsors in England
story.text: In January 1976, under Derek Dougan, Kettering became the first English club to wear a sponsor on its shirts, carrying Kettering Tyres against Bath City on 24 January. The FA ordered the logo removed and threatened a £1,000 fine. Dougan tried shortening it to Kettering T and claimed the T stood for Town. The FA were not amused and it came off, but by June 1977 they had relented and allowed sponsors' logos of up to two and a half square inches. Every shirt in English football since owes something to that afternoon.

story.title: More FA Cup goals than anyone
story.text: Kettering have scored more goals in the FA Cup than any other club in the competition's history, which takes some doing for a club outside the Football League. The best runs came in 1988-89 and 2008-09, both ending in the fourth round.

story.title: From Rockingham Road to Latimer Park
story.text: The club played at North Park, then Green Lane, before settling at Rockingham Road in 1897 and staying for over a century. In 2012 they were forced out and spent a season at Steel Park in Corby, moving to Burton Park Wanderers' ground at Latimer Park in Burton Latimer the year after. It is a long way from Rockingham Road, and plenty of supporters will tell you so.
